An invalid unload evaluator can therefore cause a nil pointer dereference. Check the error before mutating unloading."

The feature flag cannot enable SQL expressions, and the helper's name/logic are misleading. findings.title: Nil pointer dereference in reduce expression replace mode
findings.body: In ReadQuery, when a reduce query has settings.mode set to Replace but replaceWithValue is absent, the code sets err at line 83 and then dereferences q.Settings.ReplaceWithValue unconditionally at line 85. This panics before the error is returned. A malformed expression query can crash query handling. Return immediately after the nil check or only dereference when non-nil.

findings.title: Unload threshold command used before error check
findings.body: In the threshold branch, NewThresholdCommand for firstCondition.UnloadEvaluator may return an error and a nil command, but unloading.Invert is set on line 162 before err is checked on line 163. An invalid unload evaluator can therefore cause a nil pointer dereference. Check the error before mutating unloading.

findings.title: FlagSqlExpressions is ignored by always-false enablement helper
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions) and then returns false in both branches. The feature flag cannot enable SQL expressions, and the helper's name/logic are misleading. If SQL expressions are intentionally hard-disabled for security, return false explicitly and deprecate/remove the flag or update docs; otherwise this dead/inverted logic invites accidental misuse.

findings.title: No automated test locks in the SQL-expression disablement
findings.body: The PR makes QueryTypeSQL return an error and removes the DuckDB implementation, but no test is added to verify that SQL expressions are rejected, including when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. Without a regression test, a future change could silently re-enable the vulnerable SQL expression path.

findings.title: NoData result is immediately overwritten by TableData
findings.body: In SQLCommand.Execute, when frame.Rows() == 0 the code sets rsp.Values to NoData at lines 111-113, then unconditionally overwrites rsp.Values with TableData at line 116. The zero-row NoData case is therefore never returned. This is currently dormant because SQL execution is stubbed/disabled, but it will produce incorrect results if the SQL path is re-enabled.
